How sad! Well, if you ever have a need, I can get some for you. I'll check back again another time, just in case!
I've always wanted to learn leather craft. Maybe someday I can be your apprentice. If you ever need one of course! In the meantime, have a great day!

chatpoints.chat_text: That's a trade I would be happy to make -- for five pieces of leather and one leather strapping. There's a leather project I'm just itching to get started on.

replies.reply_text: I'll go get the leather now. See you in a few!
I just happen to have the leather with me!
Su Comida? I'll head there right now.

chatpoints.chat_text: Certainly! You were getting five pieces of leather for me, and one leather strapping.

replies.reply_text: That's right! I'll be back shortly.
Silly me! I've got the leather right here in my saddlebag!

chatpoints.chat_text: Jojoba oil from Su Comida. She runs the Sandy General Store.

replies.reply_text: Of course! I'll head over there now.
These look amazing! You really are a craftsman! Thanks so much and have a great day!

chatpoints.chat_text: Cowboy boots are a bit challenging. Let me think. (Hershel scratches his head and then nods.) I'll need fifteen pieces of leather and seven pieces of strapping. Unfortunately, this is a big job, so I'll need to be paid $3000 also.

replies.reply_text: Well shoot. This is more complicated than I was expecting. I might have to come back some other day. See you around!
No problem. I really need those boots and you are the only one I know of that can do the job. I've got a pirate who wants to be a cowboy and he has no boots. He wears the same size as me.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well that makes things easy. Here, step over here for a sec.

replies.reply_text: I've got the leather pieces and strapping right here in my saddlepack.
I'll go get some leather.

chatpoints.chat_text: I'm looking forward to seeing the end results. I've been thinking about creating boots for quite some time now.

replies.reply_text: I can't wait to see what you come up with. Here's the fifteen pieces of leather and seven leather strappings.
That's all I've got right now. Was there anything else you needed?
Looks like I've given you everything I've got right now. Anything else you need?

chatpoints.chat_text: Certainly. You wanted me to make cowboy boots and agreed to supply fifteen pieces of leather and seven pieces of strapping.

replies.reply_text: That's right! I've got something for you now.

chatpoints.chat_text: Of course. You'll need to get it from Su Comida.

replies.reply_text: Oh, I remember now. I'll head over there after I grab a snack to eat. See you later!
Okay, I'll be back in a few.

chatpoints.chat_text: They are indeed!

replies.reply_text: Wow! These are really special. I'm sure Scowlin' Sid will love them. Have a great day and thanks so much.

chatpoints.chat_text: Actually I do. Can you please get me some jojoba oil?

replies.reply_text: Of course!
Oh dear. I remember getting you jojoba oil in the past and it was quite a chore. I'll have to put this on hold for now. Later!
No worries. Can you remind me where to get it from?

chatpoints.chat_text: Absolutely. You were going to get me some jojoba oil.

replies.reply_text: I am on it like flies on a mudhole!
And goody, goody. I've got some right here!
Can you remind me where to get that from?

npc_list.name: Zerena
npc_list.admin_description: Quincy's widowed sister
npc_list.long_description: Zerena is an older woman with a sweet smile and welcoming nature that makes you feel right at home.

chatpoints.chat_text: Welcome. Please make yourself at home. If you need anything, don't hesitate to mention it.

replies.reply_text: Thanks. I just came in to check out the place. I'll be leaving now. Have a great day!
Thanks. Actually, I do need something. I was just talking to Barb Sower. I need a seamstress and she suggested I see you. Seems Barb has more work than she can handle at the moment.
I'm back with Farley's measurements!
Hello, Zerena! I have a need of a seamstress.
I'm back with the buttons!
Hello again. Was I doing something for you?
You don't happen to make socks, do you?
Who did you say could knit?
Was there something I was supposed to be doing for you?
I'm back with the material! And Albert said to say hi!
Thanks! I do need help, now that you mentioned it. I was wondering if you spend much time on the beach. I'm hoping you might have found half a horseshoe.

chatpoints.chat_text: (Zerena's face lights up with a warm smile.) A seamstress! I love the sound of that, although I haven't been called it in years. I didn't realize how much I missed the work until you just mentioned it. What is it that you need done?

replies.reply_text: I need to have an entire set of clothing made for someone who lives in Molten Meadows and doesn't like to travel. Is that something you'd be willing to do?
In years? What if you've forgotten how to sew? Farley's picky. Really picky! I think I'll go see if there are any other seamstresses on the isles.

chatpoints.chat_text: How exciting! An entire outfit! I would be honored to create that for your friend. I would need to charge $1200 for the outfit.

replies.reply_text: He's not my friend! That said, I would really appreciate you doing this, and I think $1200 is a fair price. You've got a deal!
Darn. That's a lot of money. I'll have to think about it. I may, or may not, be back later. See ya!
Lucky me, I've got his measurements right here.
I'll go get Farley's measurements now. Be back in a few!

chatpoints.chat_text: I can't wait to get started. An entire outfit! Remember, it will cost $1200.

replies.reply_text: Oh right! Okay, I'll be sure to bring the money with me when I pick up the outfit. Here's his measurements.
Ouch! That's costly. Let me go make some money before we agree on this proposition.
All right.  I'll remember to have the money with, but first I have to go get Farley's measurements.  I can't seem to find them here.
I'll head over there right now.

chatpoints.chat_text: Seamstress! I love the sound of that. What can I help you with today?

replies.reply_text: Darn. I forgot what I needed! Sorry to have bothered you.
I'll head over to Shellton now!

chatpoints.chat_text: Indeed you were! You were going to get me buttons from Barb Sower so I can finish up this outfit for your friend.

replies.reply_text: That's right! I'll be back shortly.
These are awesome! Farley's gonna love them. Thanks so much, and have a fantastic day!
Thanks so much for the tip! I'll head over there now.
I'll have to check with her some other time. I've got chores to run, but thanks so much for pointing me in the right direction.

chatpoints.chat_text: Yolanda.  She lives just below the apple trees. She knits all the time, and is amazing at it.

replies.reply_text: Thanks!

chatpoints.chat_text: You were going to ask Albert Junker to order some material for me.

replies.reply_text: Right you are! It slipped my mind. I'll go talk to him now.
No problem. I've got some things I need to do in Shellton, anyway.

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh dear me, no! I'm not much for the outdoors. Too much sun and seabreese for me.

replies.reply_text: I completely understand! I'll leave you be and get back to my search. Have a great day!

chatpoints.chat_text: Just because you are big does not mean that you frighten me!

replies.reply_text: Good to hear it!
No reason for you to be scared. I'm bringing you a gift!
That's fine by me! I AM scared of you! Good-bye!

chatpoints.chat_text: Really? Awesome. What is it?

replies.reply_text: I've got 2 animal balloons and a piñata for you! Your aunt Carlotta made the piñata.
I've brought your favorite thing to drink!
I've brought your favorite dessert!
Oops! Looks like I've given you everything. I'd better head back to Carlotta's now.
Oops! My mistake. I already gave it to you!
Hope you enjoy your birthday.
I've got something else!
It smells so good, it was hard not to eat any of it!
I've got something else!
Enjoy them!

chatpoints.chat_text: You aren't going to catch me and keep me in a cage are you? I'd make a really lousy pet. Seriously!

replies.reply_text: No worries! I'm not interested in having a pet tarantula!
Talking spider! Run!
Don't be silly! That's not why I'm here. I've got something to deliver to you.
I've got something for you!

chatpoints.chat_text: Something for me? Wha-hoooo!

replies.reply_text: I've got 2 animal balloons and a piñata for you! Your aunt Carlotta made the piñata.
I've brought your favorite thing to drink!
I've brought your favorite snack!
Oops! My mistake. I already gave it to you!
My mistake. I think I've given you everything.
Enjoy those!
Enjoy it!
I've got something else for you!
Smells terrific!
I've got something else for you!

chatpoints.chat_text: Could you please move aside? You are blocking the warmth from the sun.

replies.reply_text: Gosh. In this desert I think a little shade would be appreciated!
Actually, I have something for you to help make your birthday more enjoyable.
Eeeek! Spider. Run!
I've got a birthday surprise for you!

chatpoints.chat_text: I love my birthday! And I'd love to see what you've brought.

replies.reply_text: Your aunt Carlotta made you a piñata and sent along two animal balloons.
I've brought your favorite beverage.
I've brought your favorite dessert.
Nope, I'm wrong. Looks like I've already given you everything.
Oops! My mistake. I already gave it to you!
They sure make the place look festive. Enjoy them!
Sometimes, a soda just hits the spot!
I've got something else for you!
It certainly looks yummy!
I've got something else for you!

chatpoints.chat_text: Eeeek! Big scary human. I must hide!

replies.reply_text: Eeeek! Big hairy spider! Run!
No need to hide, little spider. I won't hurt  you.
Wait, I've got something to give you! Its for your birthday.
Don't hide! I've got a birthday surprise for you.

chatpoints.chat_text: Really? Oh, goodie! What is it?

replies.reply_text: I've got 2 animal balloons and a piñata for you! Your aunt Carlotta made the piñata.
I've brought your favorite thing to drink!
I've brought your favorite dessert!
Oops! Looks like I've given you everything. I'd better head back to Carlotta's now.
Oops! My mistake. I already gave it to you!
Enjoy them!
See you later!
I've got something else!
Enjoy that tasty, but sticky treat!
I've got something else!

chatpoints.chat_text: Hi there! I'm hungry. How about you? Are you packing any munchies?

replies.reply_text: (The way the tarantula is staring at you gives you the heebie jeebies. Do you think he wants to take a bite out of you?) Run!
Actually, I am! But I've got something special for you, too.
Gosh. Now that you mention it, I think I missed a meal. Time to go get something to eat.
No munchies, but I've brought you a birthday present!

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, show me what it is, already!

replies.reply_text: I've got 2 animal balloons and a piñata for you! Your aunt Carlotta made the piñata.
I've brought your favorite thing to drink!
I've brought your favorite dessert!
Silly me! Looks like I've given you everything.
Oops! My mistake. I already gave it to you!
Isn't that piñata awesome? Your Aunt Carlotta made it. I hope you enjoy it!
Milk does a body good!
I've got something else!
Enjoy that messy, but delicious treat!
I've got something else!

npc_list.name: Frederick
npc_list.long_description: This gentleman's full head of hair belies his advanced age, and he is not unhappy about it. He could easily be mistaken for a younger man except that he walks haltingly with his cane.

replies.reply_text: Back in a flash! Well, maybe more than a flash. But pretty quickly all the same.

chatpoints.chat_text: Come in, come in!

replies.reply_text: I have a special delivery from Karee Dentin, Wington's Dentist. She's new to town and wants to spread the word.
Thank you for the offer, but I can't stay. I just wanted to say hi!
Hello! You look very comfortable in that big chair.
What was I doing for you again?
I've got all your ingredients, Frederick!
I'll be sure to tell her. Have a great day.

chatpoints.chat_text: I'm thinking! Thinking very busily. Ve-ry busily.

replies.reply_text: What are you thinking about?
Well, I'll leave you to it. Would hate to interfere with the thinking process.

chatpoints.chat_text: My granddaughter's got the cold, you see. (Please do excuse her if she was rude to you when you came in- she's not at her best.) And I'd like to whip up some matzo ball soup for her. It would cure everything that ails her- old family recipe.  It's practically penicillin! But I've used up the last of my broth, and I don't think my knees are up to digging up the vegetables for a new batch.

replies.reply_text: I could get them for you. My knees have yet to complain when I bend down, so I may as well make use of them.
Huh. Well, that's a shame. I hope you can find someone to get them for you. See ya.
Matzo-what soup? What's a matzo? What's that like?

chatpoints.chat_text: Would you please? I should warn you that it will also take a trip off the isle to pick up some of the ingredients. Are you still up for it?

replies.reply_text: Oh, well, that's the case for everything I do around here, nothing's easy. I'll do it anyhow.
Never mind then.

chatpoints.chat_text: I needed... let me see. A bag of peppercorns from Rika Millgrater, a box of matzo from Ethel at the general store in Hotton, some celery and an onion from the community garden up in Wington, and then three carrots.

replies.reply_text: Right, right. I'll go off and do that.

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh, let me see, let me see! (Heaves himself out of his chair with the help of his cane.)

replies.reply_text: (Lay everything out on the table for his inspection.)
No problem! Hope your granddaughter feels better.

chatpoints.chat_text: It's like matzo ball soup! (Chuckles.) The closest thing in your experience might be a dumpling soup. Matzo is an unleavened bread; you break it up into crumbs, then bind the crumbs together to form a big ball. Those float in the broth. Try it, you'll love it!

replies.reply_text: Maybe I will! And maybe I'll get those vegetables for you.
No thanks. Good luck getting the vegetables together though.

npc_list.name: Diana
npc_list.long_description: Diana is very musically gifted. She must take after her parents! She loves flutes.

chatpoints.chat_text: I love music. Love, love, love it! And did you know that learning music helps improve math skills? It also helps the left and right brain work together in harmony.

replies.reply_text: Wow. I didn't know that!
I understand you also love flutes.

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh I do! Do you know there are many kinds of flutes?

replies.reply_text: I had no clue! Please, tell me more!

chatpoints.chat_text: I have an idea! Would you like to take a musical quiz? You'll learn about flutes and other interesting stuff that way! You give me $1000 and if you get all the questions right, I'll pay you $50,000.

replies.reply_text: Well aren't you the entrepreneur! This sounds like it could be fun. Here you go! (You hand over $1000.)
I think I'll pass for now. I need to study up before I accept your challenge.
I'm ready!
Oh gosh. I just realized I don't have time for this. Please, keep the $1000, and have a nice day. Bye!

chatpoints.chat_text:
I'll start the quiz with an easy one. Ready? This is really easy!
Which of the following is important to play the flute?

replies.reply_text: You have to have red hair.
You have to be able to blow air into the mouth piece.
You have to bite the mouth piece.
You have to know how to score music.

chatpoints.chat_text: On no! That's not the right answer. I'm sorry, I've won the challenge, but you are more than welcome to take it again.

replies.reply_text: I definitely want to try again right now. (You hand over $1000.)
I think I'll pass. My head just isn't into it right now. Thanks anyways.

chatpoints.chat_text:
(Diana giggles.) Correct!
What is someone called who plays the flute?

replies.reply_text: A flutiere
A flute tooter.
A flautist.
A wind whistler.

chatpoints.chat_text:
You got that right! They can also be called a flute player, a flutist, fluter or a flutenist. Okay, next question.
Which of the following did NOT play the flute?

replies.reply_text: Leonardo da Vinci.
George Washington.
James Madison.
Thomas Edison.

chatpoints.chat_text:
That's right! Thomas Edison played the piano. Leonardo da Vinci, George Washington and Thomas Edison all played the flute.
The flute is considered what type of instrument?

replies.reply_text: Woodwind.
Percussion.
Brass.
String.

chatpoints.chat_text:
You're right! Even though it is the only woodwind instrument that doesn't use a reed. Here's your next question.
Which of the following refers to "Sea Organ":

replies.reply_text: A funny lumpy sea creature that 'squeals' under water when it is scared.
"Sea Organ" is the name given to the organ that was in the main ballroom of the Titanic when it sank.
"Sea Organ" refers to the way the coral reefs create sound when hurricanes move over them.
"Sea Organ" is the name of a musical instrument played by the sea.

chatpoints.chat_text:
How did you know that? You're amazing! The movement of the sea pushes air through 35 musically tuned tubes on the shores of Zadar, Croatia. On to the next one.
What acoustic musical instrument has both strings like a violin and a keyboard?

replies.reply_text: The Zeusaphone - but playing it might be a hair-raising experience for you.
The Hydrolauphone - but it might be hard to play in the desert.
A Hurdy-Gurdy - but it might make you cranky.
The Singing Rain Tree - but there's not much for you to do but listen.

chatpoints.chat_text:
Way to go! A hurdy-gurdy is a wind-up musical instrument. A person who plays the hurdy-gurdy is called a hurdy-gurdyist. Next question.
What is the oldest known flute ever found?

replies.reply_text: The dudak, an Armenian double reed woodwind instrument made of apricot wood.
The panflute, which originated from the Inca and Maya civilizations.
The Gudi flute, made from the wing bones of red-crowned cranes and found in China.
The Divje Babe flute, found in the northwest region of Slovenia.
Lucky me! That was more interesting than I thought it would be. Thanks!

chatpoints.chat_text:
That's right! It is the only musical instrument associated with the Neanderthal culture and dates back to 42,000 to 43,000 thousand years ago. The Dugi was circa 9000 years ago, the Dudak was in use as early as 1500 BC, and the panflute dates between 300 and 1500 AD.
Which U.S. President played the flute?

replies.reply_text: Thomas Jefferson (1743–1826) Third president of the United States.
John Quincy Adams (1767–1848) The sixth president of the United States.
John Tyler (1790-1862) The tenth president of the United States.
Abraham Lincoln (1809-1865) The sixteenth president of the United States.

chatpoints.chat_text:
You are correct! Thomas Jefferson, John Tyler and Abraham Lincoln all played the violin.
Which famous Italian violin maker - though long deceased, has a reputation for making instruments regarded as amongst the finest bowed stringed instruments ever created?

replies.reply_text: Heinrich Englehard Steinway.
Antonio Stradivari.
Clarence Leonidas Fender.
Torakusu Yamaha.

chatpoints.chat_text:
You're amazing! Antonio Stradivari created violas, violins, cellos, guitars, harps, and mandolins. Oh my gosh. You are on your last question to a big win!
Which of the following musical instrument is considered one of the easiest to learn to play?

replies.reply_text: The Ukulele
The Accordion.
Bagpipes.
The French horn.

chatpoints.chat_text: Ding! Ding! Ding! You got it! The Ukulele is super fun to play and inexpensive to buy.

replies.reply_text: Thanks so much! Have an awesome day.

npc_list.name: Yolanda
npc_list.admin_description: New quests start at  CP#10
npc_list.long_description: Yolanda is rocking in a rocking chair and knitting. There is a basket of different colored balls of yarn at her feet.

chatpoints.chat_text: (Yolanda is smiling and rocking, knitting away.) Hello!

replies.reply_text: Hello there! Zerena told me to come see you. I need a pair of very small argyle socks. Is that something that you might be able to help me with?
Hello! Looks like you're busy, so I won't interrupt you.
That pattern that you are working on looks interesting. What kind of knitting is it?
Hello! I was wondering if you happened upon a broken horseshoe by any chance?
Sorry to bother you, but could you remind me what I was supposed to be doing for you?
I'm back! I've got that alpaca yarn for you.
Hello, Yolanda!

chatpoints.chat_text: Intarsia is knitting using different colors, creating multiple layers of separate pieces that fit together like a jigsaw puzzle and appear to be inlaid within each other.

replies.reply_text: That sounds really complicated. You must have to be really talented to do that! I'll leave you to it. Have a great day.
That's amazing! You wouldn't happen to need any more yarn or anything, would you?  I've got my heart set on a new set of tack and I need to earn some money.

chatpoints.chat_text: I love that pattern! My mother taught me the intarsia technique many years ago. That's the method I need to use to create the argyle pattern.

replies.reply_text: Whoa! This is way too much information and is just confusing me! I'll have to go rest my brain for a bit. Good bye!
That's very interesting. I really need a pair. (You tell her the measurements of Farley's feet.) Is that something you can help me with?
Intarsia technique? What's that?
Umm, he's not my friend. But, these look great! Thanks so much.

chatpoints.chat_text: Sorry, but no. I've been busy knitting and haven't been out of the cabin in days.

replies.reply_text: Okay, I'll let you get back to knitting. But you might want to think about getting some fresh air now and then.  Bye for now!

chatpoints.chat_text: Actually, I would love if you could get me some new yarn from my cousin Cecelia. If you wouldn't mind?

replies.reply_text: Certainly! I'm not sure if I remember meeting a Cecelia before. Does she live on Hoof Isle?
I remember her. She doesn't live around here. I was looking for something quick and easy. I think I'll pass on this for now. Have a good day!

chatpoints.chat_text: She lives on Dog Isle. They recently started raising a delightful little alpaca herd. Their fleece is supposed to be amazingly soft. It would be a dream yarn for baby booties.

replies.reply_text: Well, yikes. That's a heck of a lot of travel, and I was hoping for a quick chore or errand. Tell you what, if I find I have a big chunk of time on my hands, I'll reconsider. In the meantime, I'll leave you to your knitting.
That sounds interesting! Sure, I'd love to help.

chatpoints.chat_text: That's wonderful! I'm sure Cecelia will create a perfect yarn for me. If you can ask her for one skein of yarn, that would be perfect!

replies.reply_text: Happy to do that for you. I'll head over there now.

chatpoints.chat_text: Certainly! You agreed to visit my sister Cecelia on Dog Isle. She has alpaca wool that I would love to try knitting with.

replies.reply_text: That's right! I'll head over there now.

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh! This is more beautiful than I could have imagined! Thank you so much.

replies.reply_text: Happy to have helped! And thank you!

chatpoints.chat_text: (Yolanda is rocking away in the rocking chair, holding a baby bundled in a blanket). Hello.

replies.reply_text: Oh my gosh! You've had your baby! I won't interrupt, except to say congratulations! Bye now.
Hello there! Zerena told me to come see you. I need a pair of very small argyle socks. Is that something that you might be able to help me with?

npc_list.name: Charlotte
npc_list.long_description: The crab looks like some ancient fossil laying there on the sand. You wonder if it is even alive. You step closer to see....

chatpoints.chat_text: Hello? Hello? (Well looky here! There's a small horseshoe crab waving at you.)

replies.reply_text: Hello! You remind me of someone.... thinking, thinking, thinking. Yes, I've got it now! You remind me of Ebenezer. Except for you being a lot bigger than he is! I saw him on Welcome Isle.
Eeek! A crab. Run!
Well aren't you cute! (You wave back to the little critter.) Bye for now!
Hello again! Would you be so kind as to send me back to Dursley?
Hello Charlotte! I have something for you!
Hello again! Would you please call the sea turtle again? I'd like to go back to see your brother.

chatpoints.chat_text: Ah. Ebenezer. Well, yes, I would remind you of him. I'm his sister.

replies.reply_text: I'm not sure I should mention this, but he seems to be quite the grouch.

chatpoints.chat_text: He is the epitome of the name 'crab,' you might say. He has a good heart. He really does! But just to be clear, we aren't really related to crabs.

replies.reply_text: I didn't know that. Still, I'd say Ebenezer is the epitome not only in the way he acts, but his name as well!
You aren't related to crabs? Please, tell me more!

chatpoints.chat_text: Speaking of names, how rude of me not to introduce myself. I'm Charlotte.

replies.reply_text: Nice to meet you, Charlotte. What are you doing way out here in the middle of nowhere?

chatpoints.chat_text: A most unexpected wave swept me off my home island and into the ocean current. I was lost and exhausted and about to meet my fate. A kind sea-faring turtle gave me a ride to this beach.

replies.reply_text: Ah! So all's well that ends well. See ya!
Wow. That surely sounds exciting, if not a bit frightening.

chatpoints.chat_text: Indeed, it was. And lucky as well.  I much prefer this beach. The views here are delightful, and my home isle was very tiny. I saw the same old, same old day in and day out.

replies.reply_text: Just where was your home isle?
I'm so glad it turned out well for you. Have a wonderful day!

chatpoints.chat_text: (The crab gives you a long assessing look.) Would you like to go see it? I can get you a ride. For a favor of course.

replies.reply_text: What is the favor?
Oh, maybe later. I'd like to scout out this island a bit more. But thanks for asking.

chatpoints.chat_text: Would you be willing to take this message to my youngest brother, Dursley? (Charlotte waves a small piece of dried seaweed in the air.)

replies.reply_text: Of course. I'd be happy to do that. The ride you mentioned, can I leave the island that way?
Wow, look at the time. Sorry! I've got a to-do list a mile long. See ya!

chatpoints.chat_text: Yes, if you ask my brother for help.

replies.reply_text: Perfect! You just never know where you'll end up, and I like to know what I'm getting into. So, yes please. Send for the ride and I shall deliver your message!

chatpoints.chat_text: (Charlotte clicks her tail against a rock, clicking in rapid succession. There is a large swoosh from the ocean, and there, right in front of you, is a huge sea turtle.)

replies.reply_text: Thanks so much! (You wave goodbye as you ride away on the back of the sea turtle.)

chatpoints.chat_text: We are actually more closely related to scorpions and spiders and ticks.

replies.reply_text: Yuck! That's all I need to know, thank you very much anyway! Adios!

chatpoints.chat_text: Of course! (Charlotte clicks her tail against a rock, clicking in rapid succession. There is a large swoosh from the ocean, and there, right in front of you, is a huge sea turtle.)

replies.reply_text: Thank you! (You wave goodbye as you ride away on the back of the sea turtle.)
Thanks. Enjoy your dog!

npc_list.name: Grendel
npc_list.long_description: A frightful creature of some kind that looks like a cross between Big Foot and a werewolf, with a face only a mother could love.

chatpoints.chat_text: Do not darken my pathway, Stranger. Lest I be forced to sully your day. I beg of you, leave. Now.

replies.reply_text: Are you kidding me! You leave! Just make like a leaf and blow away! Ha-ha-ha!
Oh dear! Anything I can do to help?
Yikes! A scary ugly beast! Run for your lives!
Yowsers! You've got a big time need for a bath, Buddy!
Just me, again.  I'm back and I've got a huge dinosaur bone for you!
Just me, again. Could you whisk me back to the dock again?
Excuse me, Sir. I can leave as soon as you sign for this package. Special Delivery from Pony Express?
Please, Sir. I am happy to leave you be, but first I must ask for something from you that would prove you exist.

chatpoints.chat_text: Arrrggg! (With a huge swipe of his hairy paw, Grendel flings you through the air.)

replies.reply_text: Well, that wasn't the smartest thing you've done all day.

chatpoints.chat_text: Mine is a problem of epic proportions. The best thing you could do for me would be to just go away.

replies.reply_text: I can't walk away from someone in distress. Look. I'm really good at helping people and, umm, er..... Whatever. I bet I can help you if you just tell me what the problem is.
Epic proportions? Sounds way too big for me to take on. I'll just mosey on outta here!
And that's exactly what I'm going to do to help you! I'll leave. Right now!

chatpoints.chat_text: That which I desire is nothing but illusion. This, I know. Yet still, I crave it.

replies.reply_text: Okay, can you say that a different way? Pretend I haven't got a clue what you are talking about, and say it again, only differently.
Sounds like you might need to see shrink, if you know what I mean. I'll just leave you to your cravings.
And I crave a bagel! I think I'll head over to Art Isle and get one! Good-bye!

chatpoints.chat_text: I have a need that consumes me, and respite is unobtainable.

replies.reply_text: That's barely a smidgen less obtuse. How about you give it one more try?
Well that's just beyond me. Don't think I can help you at all. I'm heading out. Hope your day gets better.
Well, aren't you being the drama king!

chatpoints.chat_text: I want that which I cannot have.

replies.reply_text: That's better. What, exactly, is it that you want? Friendship? Fame? Fortune?
Join the crowd! Everyone I know wants something they can't have. I want to own the richest ranch here, but I don't! You need to just buck up and appreciate what you do have!
You're right. I can't help you. Guess I'll just leave you alone now.

chatpoints.chat_text: All of those and yet, none of those will solve my problem.

replies.reply_text: Congratulations. You've succeeded in giving me a big scary headache! No wonder you live by yourself!
Okay, enough already. I'm leaving now.
Gesh! You aren't making this any easier. Hey! How about a good meal? My mom always say a good meal makes any day better!

chatpoints.chat_text: A good meal? A temporary solution at the best, but still. That has some appeal to it.

replies.reply_text: Speaking of a good meal, I'm hungry. If I've got time, I'll try to scrounge up something for you. Later, gator!
Exactly! I'm thinking you look a bit wolfish. So I'm thinking about getting you a bone. A really big bone! What do you say?
Terrific!  I'll be back shortly!
Wow! Red pinecones! You don't see those too often. Thanks and have a better day!
I appreciate the reward. Thanks! Would you happen to know a shortcut to the dock by any chance?

chatpoints.chat_text: There you go.

replies.reply_text: Thank you! Wheeeeee!
I'm not wearing a jester's cap! No tricks here. Thanks for the pinecones and I am gone like yesterday's dessert!

chatpoints.chat_text: Exist? Who's to say? Am I here, am I not? Do I breath? Do I not? Who's to say that this life can be called an existence? Doesn't the loneliness and pain and sorrow I suffer mean I exist?

replies.reply_text: Surely the fact that we are conversing would say you exist! Let's say, for the sake of argument that you DO indeed exist. Is there something physical that you could give me that I could use as proof of your existence?
Thank you so much!

npc_list.name: Renard Junior
npc_list.admin_description: For the Earton Hunt quest. R.J. at the rocks.
npc_list.long_description: This clever fellow prides himself on having the biggest, brushiest brush-tail in all of Horse Isle- despite getting into a number of scrapes.

replies.reply_text: Renard, huh? I think I've met you before.
And look at you, proud as punch up here. What, are you just lollygagging about?
Why the heck are you getting out of the bag? I thought we were going to find your owl.
Renard, huh? I think I've met you before.
That is some impressive dentition, my friend. But your breath could use some work.

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh, you must have met my father... "Les this and les thats" Renard. He's retired from the finer things in life. Well, he'd tell you he's retired to the finer things.

replies.reply_text: And would you say the same thing?
So you're Renard's son, then?

chatpoints.chat_text: Nah. (Gives you a big foxy grin.) I'm an adventurer, myself. And it's a beautiful thing.

replies.reply_text: Adventurer, huh? Do your adventures take you in the way of foxhounds, by any chance?
A beautiful thing, to distract the hounds and take them all over hill and dale? Sound familiar?

chatpoints.chat_text: (Makes a low rumble deep in his throat that you realize is actually a laugh.) That's me! To tell you the truth, I've got a bet running.

replies.reply_text: A bet? What does a fox need with a bet? And with whom did you even make it?

chatpoints.chat_text: With Orly, the owl down south by the scraggly tree in all the fuzz. He bet me I couldn't pull the hounds off their tracks today. I bet him I sure could! I'm just biding my time, but I've got work to do today.

replies.reply_text: But... they've laid an easy track out today with the drag. It's little kids. If you take the hounds off the scent and really take them on a run, the kids might get hurt.

You just go on with yourself there.

chatpoints.chat_text: I have a terrible. Horrible. No good. Very bad. ITCH! (Looks at you in a most pathetic manner.) The life of an outlaw, it is not an easy one. N'est-ce pas?

replies.reply_text: Well, that settles it. You've got to be one of Renard's kids.
He's doing well, all things considered, outside of the fact that he has four kids who apparently never send a message home.

chatpoints.chat_text: I do feel bad about that. And me being his favorite son, too. I'd be his favorite child, but he was always inordinately fond of my youngest sister. Between you and me, friend, she is thoroughly addle-pated. But Dad's doing okay, you said?

replies.reply_text: All things considered, like I said. He seems to be enjoying his retirement very much.
I think he's doing well, but a little lonely for contact with his kids.

chatpoints.chat_text: I miss that old dog. I wanted to leave home for sure, it was getting a little claustrophobic with all of us. But you wouldn't believe how hard it is to stow back away in a ship! I guess I got off of Aesop by luck. Like everything else!

replies.reply_text: Well, do you want me to take a message back from you?
Do you want me to tell him how you're doing?

chatpoints.chat_text: Tell him I'm doing all right! Living by my wits, such as they are. (He winks.) Say, can I send you back with something? A token of my esteem for the old dog?

replies.reply_text: Sure, what did you have in mind?
Sure, that's easy enough. I'll take that to him along with your message.

chatpoints.chat_text: You have no idea.

replies.reply_text: I probably don't.

chatpoints.chat_text: In the wishing well, of course! Lean right over and peer right in.

replies.reply_text: Oh, right. I guess I'll have to look pretty close up.

npc_list.name: Zachava
npc_list.long_description: Zachava is a joyful young mother who obviously adores her daughter. Both she and her daughter have gorgeous golden hair that is hard not to notice!

chatpoints.chat_text: Hello. Welcome to our humble cabin.

replies.reply_text: Thanks! I noticed that you and Hannah have the same golden hair color. Its a beautiful shade.
Thank you. I was wondering if you had any errands that need to be done? I'm trying to make some money for this awesome set of tack I want to buy.
What was I doing for you again?
Thank you! I'm here from Cadence to pick up your seed contribution for the garden.
Hello and thank you. I understand I need to contact you about the community gardens?
What did you say about those soup ingredients that I was looking for?

chatpoints.chat_text: Sounds like a worthy goal! I do have an errand, if you think you have time. It requires a bit of travel.

replies.reply_text: Oh, no worries. I'm used to traveling! What is it that you need done?
Darn. I was hoping for a quick errand, here on the island. Well, maybe I can help you another time. Bye!

chatpoints.chat_text: We do! It's a family trait. As far back as we can tell, the women in my family have the golden hair. Until it turns gray, of course!

replies.reply_text: Well, it certainly is lovely. Have a great day!

chatpoints.chat_text: Patience has been wearing a lovely sea shell necklace. I'd like to get two, one for Hannah and one for me. Hannah loves for us to be dressed alike.

replies.reply_text: What a great idea! And I know just where to get those necklaces. I'll be back soon.

So you like that twinkie-twin look, huh? Well, everyone has their own tastes, I guess. You know, I just remembered I've got some chores to tend to. Maybe I can come back and help you out some other day. Bye!
I'll be back shortly!
Actually, I have two with me!
Thanks so much! See ya!

chatpoints.chat_text: You were going to bring me two seashell necklaces.

replies.reply_text: Silly me! I've got them right here!
That's right! I'll be back in a jiffy.
That sounds lovely!

chatpoints.chat_text: You can get the potatoes and beets from the community garden. William at the Inn usually has plenty of onions and cabbage. And Cadence has carrots in her garden.

replies.reply_text: That's right! And the sour cream?

chatpoints.chat_text: Yes, yes! It is such a pleasure to be part of this community! I volunteered to start the gardens and everyone just chips in and helps. Are you volunteering to weed or fertilize them?

replies.reply_text: Ummm. I hadn't planned on doing either. I was hoping to get some vegetables from it. Baba Yaga wants to make borscht.

chatpoints.chat_text: Baba Yaga? I see. (Zachava chews on the corner of her lip for just a moment, then breaks into a smile.) Of course. What do you need?

replies.reply_text: Baba Yaga wants four beets, three carrots, two potatoes, one onion and one head of cabbage.

chatpoints.chat_text: Help yourself to the potatoes and beets from the garden. Cabbage and onions are out of season. Check with William at the Inn. He should have some. And Cadence has carrots in her garden.

replies.reply_text: Thank you so much. Oh, would you know where I could get some sour cream?

chatpoints.chat_text: Is it Cookie that you can get milk from? I can't remember. Anyway, one of the three sisters on Jungle Isle can help you with that.

replies.reply_text: Thanks so much!

npc_list.name: Justin
npc_list.admin_description: NEW QUESTS CP15 Dalton's adopted grandson (because despite having had a grandson for years, he's never actually had one...)
npc_list.long_description: Justin is a strapping lad who wants to be a blacksmith when he grows up. He'll tell you this despite the fact that, judging by his deep voice and altitude, he's already grown pretty far up.

chatpoints.chat_text: Yes, he's relapsed again. He's always had trouble with his lungs, and now it's getting worse.

replies.reply_text: But I thought he was doing better! I brought him medicine and everything! He said he was feeling much improved!
Oh no, what do the doctors say?

chatpoints.chat_text: (Justin is cooking soup on a small old stovetop.)

replies.reply_text: Excuse me, Justin, but your grandfather... He doesn't seem well.
Yum, that smells delicious.
I'm pretty sure you can go back to making soup for one for a week or so...
That smells delicious, Justin. What was I doing for you again?

chatpoints.chat_text: They're not really sure what to do for him at this point. They say the best we can do is make him comfortable.

replies.reply_text: Oh, I'm so sorry. Is it just the coughing? Is there something else going on?
I'm very sorry to hear it. I'll leave you alone now. It doesn't seem to be a good time for visitors.

chatpoints.chat_text: (He lowers his voice.) Honestly, I don't think Gramps is entirely lucid right now. He seems like he's totally with it, but he keeps talking about some misty island he went to for an autumn rest cure when he was younger. It doesn't sound really... real.

replies.reply_text: What about it doesn't seem real?
I've been to plenty of fantastical places like you wouldn't believe. Give me a try.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, for one thing, there was a unicorn. (He sighs.) I don't know what to do. I can give him soup and read him books to keep his mind off it, and I've managed to keep the garden going so he can enjoy his fresh veggies, but I'm worried.

replies.reply_text: What about finding this magical island? If he believes it cured him once...
I can see why you would be.

chatpoints.chat_text: Frankly, I think it would be a total waste of time. Unicorns and pink rabbits and talking stars... they just don't exist in the real world. I wish they did. Maybe they could help him.

replies.reply_text: Look, it's clear that you can't leave here, because you have to take care of him. But I've seen crazier things than unicorns and pink rabbits in my time. Maybe I can help you find this island.

chatpoints.chat_text: It can't hurt... It's just that if he really believes he went to some magic land... I don't want to get his hopes up when it doesn't actually exist.

replies.reply_text: Okay, so we'll keep it just between the two of us. If the island really exists, I'll find it, and if not, no harm done since your granddad won't know we went looking for it.
You're right. Maybe it's not such a good idea.

chatpoints.chat_text: I think that's the best way. Here. (He hands you a child's picture drawn in crayon.) Gramps says this is the way he traveled to the island. He drew the picture when he was a kid.

replies.reply_text: Well, let me take a look at it and see what I can see.

chatpoints.chat_text: You were going off to see if you can find the magical island where Gramps was cured as a child. I take it you haven't found it yet.

replies.reply_text: Not yet, no.
Not yet. But I'm sure that if I put my head on it, I can figure it out.
I have, actually! I haven't quite gotten an answer for you yet... but I thought you should know that the isle exists!

chatpoints.chat_text: It goes in stages. He'll have good times and bad times. This is one of the bad spells.

replies.reply_text: Oh, I'm sorry to hear it. I didn't realize he was this ill. What do the doctors say?

chatpoints.chat_text: Yeah, I figured.

replies.reply_text: I'm going to keep looking, though. Like you said, it can't hurt.

chatpoints.chat_text: Thanks, it's Gramps' favorite- matzo ball soup. Practically penicillin.

replies.reply_text: You're so right about that!
Never heard of it.

chatpoints.chat_text: I guess the familiarity is going to give me some comfort. I can't say I expected all this to end with a dragon flying my grandfather out the front door!

replies.reply_text: No, I can see how you wouldn't quite expect that. Are you worried about how this all ended up going? I know everything was a bit... sudden. And unusual.

chatpoints.chat_text: No, I'm thrilled. Maybe I should have taken Gramps seriously about that whole magic isle business, but it just seemed so completely fantastic that it couldn't be real!

replies.reply_text: You'll have to go see the Isle of Hardly for yourself! There's a Luckdragon on Turtle Isle who will probably take you over whenever you like, if you say you're Dalton's grandson. You can visit him often until he comes home.

chatpoints.chat_text: Thank you, I'll want to do that. Can't quite let the old man out of my sight.  I just can't believe it's all real quite yet! Thank you, thank you, thank you, for all you did for my grandfather. It really does seem like a magic cure!

replies.reply_text: You're very welcome!

chatpoints.chat_text: Hello!

replies.reply_text: Hi Justin! How's your grandfather doing? Heard from him lately?

chatpoints.chat_text: Doing much better! I was over there on the Isle of Hardly yesterday. It's a wonderful place! Gramps should be ready to come home soon, but I can't imagine we won't both be visiting the Isle a lot in the future!

replies.reply_text: That's great! I'm so glad to hear he's well again.

chatpoints.chat_text: Really now... well, keep me posted. If you can make anything of this, I'll owe you. (Looks over at his grandfather, whose racking coughs have gotten worse.) I hate seeing him like this and not being able to help.

replies.reply_text: I will.

npc_list.name: Pearl
npc_list.admin_description: Pearl on Octavius's quest
npc_list.long_description: A very large clam with a long neck.

replies.reply_text: And you have a very nice day.

chatpoints.chat_text: And what are YOUUUUUUUU doing?!

replies.reply_text: ACK! Giant clam! Uh... I'm digging up some coral, Miss Giant Clam. Deidra said I could.
Uh... just came back to ask you where to find that algae again.
I'm back with the algae and the pearls for you.

chatpoints.chat_text: Digging up coral! For shame! Didn't your mother ever teach you to respect your environment? Don't you know coral is a precious and rapidly-dwindling resource?

replies.reply_text: ...that's some big words for a clam.
I do know, and that's why Deidra told me to get some here, where she was farming it, rather than from one of the reefs.

chatpoints.chat_text: What, you think that just because I live in a shell I can't have a good vocabulary? Humph! You're a presumptuous little thing, aren't you?

replies.reply_text: Look, I'm sorry. You just surprised me. When Deidra told me to dig here to take a sample of the coral, I wasn't expecting to be shrieked at by a clam.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, IF you want me to give you a little of this coral, you'll be bringing me back some algae! Coral of this type can't live without it- the algae feeds the coral and the coral gives it somewhere to live. If you want some coral, you'll have to help me grow more!

replies.reply_text: I thought this was Deidra's coral farm. She told me I could take some. Why should I bring you anything?

chatpoints.chat_text: Deidra, hmm? And who do you see taking care of this coral now, huh? NOT Deidra!

replies.reply_text: Okay... so where can I find the right kind of algae?
For putting up with me?! Really!

chatpoints.chat_text: You take some putting up with!

replies.reply_text: Well, if that isn't calling the kettle black!

chatpoints.chat_text: Forgot already?! Humans these days! You're going to the southeast point of Jungle Isle and looking under the double palm tree. And don't you forget to come back with my twenty pearls either!

replies.reply_text: Thanks for repeating yourself, Miss Pearl.

npc_list.name: Christel
npc_list.admin_description: Toymaker, sells jacks-in-box
npc_list.long_description: Christel and her grandmother Hanska both will tell you that Christel learned absolutely everything she knows from Hanska, with two exceptions. One is her needlework (abysmal, despite Hanska's best efforts) and her welding (exemplary, thanks to the blacksmith who lived next door to her childhood home.)

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh, hello there!

replies.reply_text: Hi!  Say, what are all those boxes in the corner?
Hi! I would like to buy a jack-in-the-box please. ( Hand over $50.)
Hi!  Just passing through.  Bye!
Hello, I have a proposition for you.
Hello there! Would you be the doll maker that lives on this island?

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh, over there? (Motions to the corner where a pile of brightly painted boxes with crank handles are neatly stacked.) Those are jack-in-the-boxes. I made quite a few a while back. Sort of for practice and for fun.

replies.reply_text: Oh really?  Would I be able to buy one?  They look neat.  Maybe my horse would like it.
Well, that seems like an awful waste of time....  Have fun with those.  Bye.

chatpoints.chat_text: Sure, if you want, though I would think most horses wouldn't like them.  You can always try though I guess.  They're not that great, so if you want one I'm fine with you just paying $50.

replies.reply_text: Yeah, you're probably right.  I guess I'll pass.
That's quite a steal!  I'll take one!
I'm sure it will be fine.  Thanks!

chatpoints.chat_text: You have a proposition for us?  What is it?

replies.reply_text: Iona, over in Flipperton, wants to hold a Founder's Day Crafts Festival.  She's hoping you can attend and display your work.  Here's your invitation.
I'll let Iona know. Take care!

chatpoints.chat_text: Not me. I haven't learned those skills yet. But I'm great at making Jack-in-the-boxes! Would you like to buy one?

replies.reply_text: Sure! I like to support local businesses.
Well drat. Thanks for you time, and no thank you on the toy.

npc_list.name: Hanska
npc_list.admin_description: Christel's grandmother. Master toymaker. Retired.
npc_list.long_description: Hanska is a tiny woman whose posture suggests a backbone of steel. Her gray hair is pinned up in an enormous bun; she hasn't cut it since her last ballet performance over 60 years ago.

chatpoints.chat_text: Hello, dear. What brings you here?

replies.reply_text: Just visiting.
I was looking for someone to make some toys for me.
I'm just wandering around, thank you. But you look a little upset. Is something the matter?
Hanska, remind me what I was doing for you?
Hanska, remind me what I was doing for you?
Hanska, I've read that letter that Jack left you, and I'm sorry, but it doesn't mean a thing to me.
Hanska, I wanted to let you know- I've found some clues. I don't know if they'll lead to anything, but I'm going to try.
Hanska... I have two things for you. One is your toy soldier. The other is this sack- it's full of letters Jack wrote you. They were never able to be delivered, but she never stopped writing you.
Hello.  I'm here with a propositon for you.
I was just looking ar... Oooo, what's over there? (You point to plush pegasi and unicorns sitting on a shelf.)
I was just stopping by to see if you've had any new projects lately.
I was coming to buy a plush unicorn companion for my horse.  It was $250, right?
I wanted to buy a plush pegasus companion for my horse.  It was $250, right?
I am on a mission to buy a new doll for a young girl. I see you are a master toymaker. Can you help me?
I came because I wanted to buy a plush triceratops.  They look so cute!

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh, you'll want to talk to my granddaughter for that. I've retired, you see. Quite a few years ago!

replies.reply_text: Oh. Well, what kind of toys did you make when you were still in business?
Oh. I guess you can't make teddy bears and whatnot forever.
Okay, I'll go talk to her.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, I specialized, you know. I didn't do toys so much as I did figurines. Have you ever painted a model replica, dear?

replies.reply_text: Yes, I've done that a time or two.
No, I can't say I have.

chatpoints.chat_text: Then you know how perfect it feels to get it just right! I enjoy that feeling.

replies.reply_text: What made you stop?

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, surely you know how satisfying it feels to do a tricky thing right! I loved that feeling.

replies.reply_text: Why did you stop, then?

chatpoints.chat_text: Arthritis, you know. We all have to slow down sometime, I suppose.

replies.reply_text: I guess. It must be hard for you to be up in this climate, isn't it?
I guess we do. Well, I've got to get going.
You don't make anything at all anymore?

chatpoints.chat_text: Yes, the cold certainly doesn't help anything, but I think you ought to live somewhere you have connections. My granddaughter and I just moved to the Horse Isles together, and Kelda next door is a very dear friend. Her son and Christel have an understanding, you know.

replies.reply_text: Do they really?

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, they don't presently, but mark my words, dear, they will. Trust me, I'm old, I know these things.

replies.reply_text: I'll take your word for it.
I've heard that from my own grandmother. She told me "You'll like your sister one day. Trust me, I'm old, I know these things." She was right...
I've heard that from my own grandmother. She told me "You'll like your sister one day. Trust me, I'm old, I know these things." I'm still waiting...

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, yes, but on very, very rare occasions. It must be a very, very special project.

replies.reply_text: Oh, I see. Well, I'll keep that in mind.

chatpoints.chat_text: Why, dearie, what makes you say that?

replies.reply_text: Well, for one, you look like you've been crying...
The soaked handkerchiefs next to you are sort of a clue.
I'm just very good at reading faces.

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh, thank you for your concern. I think I might just be being a bit of a silly old lady about it.

replies.reply_text: A silly lady about what in particular?
Okay...

chatpoints.chat_text: My missing toy soldier. (She gestures to her windowsill.)

replies.reply_text: I don't see a toy soldier on your windowsill...
Oh, I'm sorry. I hope you find it soon.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well yes, dearie, I did say it was missing. (She sighs.) It's very silly of me, but I'm afraid that means the worst.

replies.reply_text: I'm not sure I'm following.
What means the worst? What's "the worst" that could happen to a toy soldier?

chatpoints.chat_text: I suppose I should back up. I was a prima ballerina in my youth, you know. (She touches her considerable bun of iron-gray hair.) Well, I was until I injured my knee, and after that I retired to toys, but I digress. In tours with my company, I met my very good friend Jack, and we stayed in touch for many years. We were each traveling with our respective companies, but we made a point of seeing each other whenever we were both in the same town. Then we each got hurt around the same time. I retired here to toymaking, but Jack- in the coast guard, you know- got what I understood to be a very good job offer- mind, never told me what it was... Working with ships, anyway. Well, we both moved at the same time, and one thing and another, we didn't have each other's addresses. So I haven't heard from my friend Jack since...

replies.reply_text: I'm sorry to hear that, but I don't think I understand what that has to do with your toy soldier.
Why haven't you contacted Jack's family or friends? Surely SOMEBODY knows where your friend moved to.

chatpoints.chat_text: Yes, yes, I was getting there. When I was just starting out as a toy maker, I crafted a toy ballerina and a toy soldier- the ballerina was me, of course, and the toy soldier was Jack. We'd mail them back and forth to each other with each letter, and when Jack sent me that last letter, they were included in the parcel. They sat together on my window ledge for many, many years, even after Jack and I lost touch. But now my soldier has disappeared, and I fear that means the worst.

replies.reply_text: Oh... are you thinking that because the soldier represents Jack and the soldier has fallen out of sight, that Jack may have passed away?
So you think that the loss of your soldier means that Jack has passed? (Privately you think this is a bit of a stretch.)

chatpoints.chat_text: Yes, my dear, I'm afraid that that's exactly what has happened. (She sighs deeply, staring at the lone ballerina on the window ledge.) If I only knew where Jack had settled, I could make enquiries, but these things are so difficult...

replies.reply_text: Well, if you'll forgive me saying so, I might be a better person to look than you- fresh eyes and all that. Maybe I can help you. You said you had one last letter from Jack- did that have any hints about where your friend might have gone?
I'm sorry for your difficulties. I hope you can find an answer soon.

chatpoints.chat_text: I've gone over and over this letter- the last I received from Jack- for many years now, and it's told me nothing about where my friend settled. Maybe you can make more of it.

replies.reply_text: I'll give it a read.

chatpoints.chat_text: Have you read Jack's letter yet? Maybe it will tell you something. It's told me nothing all these years.

replies.reply_text: Oh... no, I haven't. I'll read through it now.
I did, but I'm afraid I can't make heads or tails out of it.

chatpoints.chat_text: It's a pity. I certainly hope I'm wrong about that soldier. Perhaps I'll never know...

replies.reply_text: Well, I can always keep investigating. Things don't fall out of windows for no reason, after all.

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh... then you haven't found anything? You said you'd keep investigating to see if you could find out where my toy soldier has gone.

replies.reply_text: I guess I can take another look outside.

chatpoints.chat_text: Thank you, dear. I hope you can find something to set my heart at rest. That's so like Jack- never a straight answer. But if you have troubles getting your own thoughts straight, no wonder you can't do the same in writing... But I'm rambling, aren't I?

replies.reply_text: You're remembering. That's all right. I hope I can find an answer for you.

chatpoints.chat_text: Unfortunately, no. One of the things that Jack and I had in common is that we'd both lost our parents a relatively young ages. Our companies became our families.

replies.reply_text: Well, if your companies- I guess your ballet corps and Jack's division in the Navy- became your families, did you ever try to contact Jack's?

chatpoints.chat_text: I tried that, but I never got an answer- I suppose there was no way to prove to them that I'd known Jack for a long time and wasn't trying to get information I had no right to know.

replies.reply_text: That's frustrating, but I guess I can see where that would have been the case, if you weren't related. Anyway, what does all of this have to do with your missing toy soldier?

chatpoints.chat_text: A whole sack?! But... why weren't they delivered?! All this time...

replies.reply_text: They couldn't deliver them- none of the letters were addressed with enough information to get to you. It was the same problem you had getting letters to her.

chatpoints.chat_text: But she'd been addressing these letters like this our whole lives! (She pulls out a large basket of letters to show you.) "To Hanska Hennig, Sujet, Whiskerton Ballet Corps." This one is quite old.

replies.reply_text: Apparently Whiskerton didn't have a forwarding address for you either.

chatpoints.chat_text: She wrote me all these years... I thought she'd given up... My, my... (She swallows back what you suspect are tears.) Thank you, my dear. You've made an old woman very happy... and very sad at the same time, but that's not your fault. Thank you.

replies.reply_text: I'll leave you alone to read them.

chatpoints.chat_text: Of course they didn't, I haven't lived in Whiskerton since I was a child... So you say that all of this was because of a misunderstanding about where to deliver the letters?!

replies.reply_text: I'm afraid so.

chatpoints.chat_text: What sort of proposition do you have in mind?

replies.reply_text: Iona, over in Flipperton, wants to hold a Founder's Day Crafts Festival.  She's hoping you can attend and display your work

chatpoints.chat_text: I'm sorry, I don't travel much any more.  Ask Christel if she'd like to attend on our behalf.

replies.reply_text: Okay, I'll ask her.  Thank you for your time.

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh those?  I've been trying to keep my hands busy by sewing up some plush unicorns and pegasi.  They are fun to make.

replies.reply_text: Would you be willing to sell one?  I think my horse would love that!
Very neat.  Well, I'm glad you're keeping busy.  I'll leave you be now.  Bye.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, sure.  I'll sell either one. I have no use for them here.  I'll sell one for $250.

replies.reply_text: That's a bit much for me.  Maybe another time.
I'll take a unicorn!
I'll buy a pegasus!
Thanks!
Thanks!

chatpoints.chat_text: I can't, but I'm sure our lovely neighbor Kelda can help you.

replies.reply_text: Thank you so much for letting me know. Have a wonderful day.

chatpoints.chat_text: Funny timing!  I've actually started branching out in trying my hand at other plush animals.  Dinosaurs, to be exact.  I currently only have a triceratops.

replies.reply_text: That sounds so neat!  I love dinosaurs!  How much are you selling them for?
That's too bad.  I'm not really a fan of dinos.  Good luck though!
That's great!  Thanks for letting me know.  I'll keep it in mind.
I would love a triceratops.
Thanks!  I'm sure it will.

npc_list.name: Polly
npc_list.admin_description: Whorl Isle
npc_list.short_description: a woman who sees the bigger picture
npc_list.long_description: Polly is a particularly matter-of-fact woman. Her friends call her 'Oliver.' None of them have elected to explain why.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well?

replies.reply_text: Uh... what?
Nothing.

Honestly, I'm worried about your friend Mal over there. She seems a little... out of it. On edge. Behaving bizarrely. In need of an exorcism. I don't know how you want to phrase it, but I'm concerned about her, and possibly also your safety.
Well, I'm back with the acorns, that's swell.
Well, I forgot how I was helping Mal. And you. But Mal seems in need of most help.
Well, I forgot how I was helping Mal. And you. But Mal seems in need of most help.
Well, I forgot how I was helping Mal. And you. But Mal seems in need of most help.
Well, I brought Mal's coffee shipment back from the dock.
I gave Mal the acorn stuff, and she didn't short-circuit, so I guess that's something?
Well, I was wondering if you'd been fishing lately.
You'd sent me to a Marina... who's Marina?

chatpoints.chat_text: What do you mean, what?

replies.reply_text: I mean what. You asked me a question with no context, and I asked you to clarify.
I mean just that. I meant what I said and I said what I meant. And what I meant was, "What?"

chatpoints.chat_text: Are you trying to be smart with me?

replies.reply_text: No!
I guess so.
Absolutely.

chatpoints.chat_text: Listen here, you: if you're not trying to be smart, you are trying to be stupid! I'll only ask you once more! Are you trying to be smart with me?

replies.reply_text: I guess I am trying to be smart!
...I think there's no right answer here.

chatpoints.chat_text: Better than the alternative!

replies.reply_text: Uh... yes ma'am.

chatpoints.chat_text: Are you saying that you think she's behaving like she's stark raving mad with an uninhibited anger management problem, is that it?

replies.reply_text: Uh... I really hate to say it, but yes, that's what I'm saying.

That sounds awful to live with. Why haven't you just ordered more coffee?
Oh, the poor soul. I can't imagine a life without coffee. Have you ordered more?

chatpoints.chat_text: I already have. Her shipment was supposed to be in at the dock late last night, but the boat was delayed leaving Tropicton because of the foul weather there, and won't have gotten in to our local dock yet.

replies.reply_text: And in the meantime she's clearly experiencing withdrawal. Isn't there something else you can give her in the meantime to offset the cravings?
That's rough. Best of luck dealing with it.

chatpoints.chat_text: Actually, now that you mention it, I do remember something I picked up from my grandmother. She was in the military- bit of a family tradition there- and she said that when her unit ran out of coffee and had no resupply, they used... now what was it...

replies.reply_text: Waiting for it...

chatpoints.chat_text: ACORNS! That was it. It doesn't have any caffeine, of course, but my grandmother said it tasted similar enough that it kept them from going too crazy without their morning cuppa. Although in her case- (Polly jerks her head towards Mal, who is possibly hallucinating in a corner.) -it's more like the every-two-hours cuppa.

replies.reply_text: I was actually thinking about something like tea, that has caffeine in it... but I guess acorns will work just as well. Exactly as well. How about I go get you a couple, then, and we can see how it works?

chatpoints.chat_text: By the time you get back with all of them, hopefully the boat will have come in, and I can get her stabilized on this while we wait on you to pick up the order.

replies.reply_text: Fifty acorns?! Yikes. Is this person a person or a squirrel?

chatpoints.chat_text: (Looking haggard, as though the time since you last saw her has been spent fighting some great battle.) Great. I'll just have to grind those up and serve.

replies.reply_text: I hope it works.  Here are the acorns.

chatpoints.chat_text: If she will just avoid setting the house on fire while she drinks this, it will have done its job.

replies.reply_text: Setting the house on fire?! That's alarming... Okay, I'll go give this to her.

chatpoints.chat_text: She's considerably more coherent. I should be able to hold down the fort here until you get back from the dock with the coffee she ordered. The boat should be in by now. Give the bag straight to Mal when you get back.

replies.reply_text: I thought I was just getting you acorns! Grumble, grumble...
I can understand. When I really want a cup of coffee, I really want a cup of coffee. And it looks like Mal is well past that point...

chatpoints.chat_text: You were collecting acorns. Fifty of them. She drinks a lot of coffee.

replies.reply_text: That's a lot of acorns.

chatpoints.chat_text: You were getting her coffee shipment from the dockmistress here on Whorl. If you've already done that, take it straight to Mal, or she might attack you for it.

replies.reply_text: That sounds dangerous. Okay.

chatpoints.chat_text: You were making sure she gets her mouth on some of this acorn coffee substitute. It looks like it tastes dire. I hope it works.

replies.reply_text: The way it smells, I'm kind of afraid to offer it to her, but I guess I'll take this one for the team...

chatpoints.chat_text: What are you doing?! Go give that to Mal! She's going to attack you for it! Hurry!

replies.reply_text: Eep!

chatpoints.chat_text: You know, it's funny you ask that.. I found the strangest thing the other day.

replies.reply_text: Strange in what way?
That seems like a non-sequitur, but okay, I'll go with it...

chatpoints.chat_text: I was preparing a fish for dinner, and I found the strangest thing in its stomach. It was a toy tin soldier. But you know what was stranger?

replies.reply_text: Go on, tell me!

chatpoints.chat_text: It looked exactly like my Grandma Jack.

replies.reply_text: ...Grandma Jack. That was not what I expected to hear.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, if your name was Jacqueline, you could perfectly well be a Jack, too. She was in the navy for years, until she had to retire because of her leg; then the coast guard offered her a position as the dock master here, and my family's been here ever since.

replies.reply_text: I can solve half your mystery... the toy soldier looks like your grandmother because it was made to. I've been looking for the soldier for awhile now, actually. It was made by a lady named Hanska on Polar Isle.

chatpoints.chat_text: Hanska? That must be Hans. Grandma used to tell us stories about the two of them when they were younger. They were best of friends. I always wondered why they lost touch. I'd have liked to meet her.

replies.reply_text: Hanska said your grandmother wrote her a letter when she was about to move here, but it didn't have an address on it. For that matter, I don't think your grandmother knew where to find Hanska- she moved, too. Do you know when they lost touch?

That's so strange. Hanska said your grandmother never left her a forwarding address. So she couldn't have written back. And I don't think your grandmother ever knew where Hanska was moving, either. Do you know when they lost touch?

chatpoints.chat_text: No, I really don't. It was around the time she met my grandfather, I know. She sent Hans an invitation to the wedding, but Hans didn't come. Didn't even respond, and of course Grandma sent an address for RSVP. It made Grandma Jack wonder, I can tell you. In fact she was worried that Hans had stopped responding because she was ill or dead!

replies.reply_text: That's what Hanska thought when her toy soldier went missing. She thought it was some kind of cosmic sign.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, I'm afraid she was right about that... my grandmother passed away not so long ago. But that is just so strange. I know Grandma Jack sent her more letters. But you say they never got to Hanska? Just strange.

replies.reply_text: It's bizarre. From what I've heard from you and Hanska, it sounds like there's no reason for them to have stopped writing. I wonder if their letters got lost somehow?
That's so sad. And it doesn't make any sense. They were lifelong friends- why would they just lose touch like that, especially if your grandmother kept writing?
Thanks. I hope there's something. At this point I'm just so curious.

chatpoints.chat_text: (Impatiently.) Marina at the dock. Do you know another Marina?

replies.reply_text: No. Thank you.

npc_list.name: Mal
npc_list.admin_description: Mal, on Whorl Isle. Extremely androgynous. Possibly a vampire. I love Terry Pratchett.
npc_list.long_description: Mal is a rather batlike person: inclined to be nocturnal and fond of sleeping with her head rather lower to the ground than her feet. Woe betide anyone who steps between her and a cup of coffee.

chatpoints.chat_text: Mornin'. Coffee...

replies.reply_text: Good morning. How are you?
It's not really morning...
I've got something like that for you.
I've got it. I've got it. I've got your coffee. Take it and stop scaring me please.

chatpoints.chat_text: I just woke up. It's morning. Where's my coffee?

replies.reply_text: It's right here.
(You look around, but don't see anything resembling a coffee cup.) I don't see it.
I'm working on it. I am. Promise.

chatpoints.chat_text: (Very nearly wails.) Myyyyy coffeeeeee!

replies.reply_text: ...I don't think I can help you with this problem.
Can I help you with this?
Calm down. It's going to be okay. How about some nice tea?

chatpoints.chat_text: Ahh. (Downs a "cup" of coffee that's more akin to the size of a flower vase.) That's better. I feel... slightly human. Want one?

replies.reply_text: Sure! Thanks.
Got any tea, by chance?
Cheers!

chatpoints.chat_text: I do not drink... tea.

replies.reply_text: Well, I do.

chatpoints.chat_text: Eh. Where's my coffee?

replies.reply_text: It's right here.
(You look around, but don't see anything resembling a coffee cup.) I don't see it.

chatpoints.chat_text: Coffeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee.

replies.reply_text: Uh... right?
What about it?

chatpoints.chat_text: COFFEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!

replies.reply_text: Yes, you said that already...
Can you elaborate on what it is you want me to do for you? Using more than just one word, maybe?
I am alarmed and I am getting out of here.
Uh. I'm going to go talk to your friend over there. Maybe she can help me. Also, you scare me.
...I don't speak your language. I'm going to go see if your friend thinks that that did the trick.
Man, am I glad THAT is over.

npc_list.name: Edward
npc_list.admin_description: Olivia's grandson. Polar Isle.
npc_list.long_description: Edward is quite small for his age, and between his height and his dreamy personality, he sometimes gets picked on. He has thus learned to be the fastest runner in his grade.

chatpoints.chat_text: (Scribbling quickly in a somewhat illegible hand, talking to himself as he does so.) The Baron advanced, holding up his pike, but brave Brunhilda refused to back down. She would defend her friend the- (Frowns, then raises his voice to call across the cabin.) Grandma, how do you spell 'marchioness'?

replies.reply_text: That's a big word for somebody your age!
M-A-R-C-H-I-O-N-E-S-S.
I have no idea what that even means! Kids with bigger vocabularies than mine make me uneasy. See ya!
What was I doing for you?
I was doing something for you, right?
What was I doing for you?
Hey buddy. I'm afraid I have bad news. Ted said he wasn't looking for an apprentice right now.
I've got news for you! Ted says he doesn't need an apprentice, but he'll read your novel when you're done it, and give you some tips!
Hey Edward. I don't suppose you have that castle down on the shore, do you?
Edward, where did you say you thought the paper boat and toy soldier might have gone?

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh! You scared me! I didn't even know you were there!

replies.reply_text: Sorry, I didn't mean to make you jump. What is it you're working on?

chatpoints.chat_text: It's my Novel. (You can hear the capital letter.) I'm almost done, too. This is the big fight, where Brunhilda, Duchess of Winter's March, fends off the evil Baron who wants to marry her friend Ermengarde. And then he'd kill Ermengarde so that he could have her lands, see? If Brunhilda can hold off the Baron for just ten minutes, her faithful knights will be able to get there in time, and they'll win the fight. Brunhilda knows they're only a little ways away.

replies.reply_text: Wow! That sounds like an exciting fight. How do you come up with all your scenes?

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh, I act them out. (Gestures at a big box of crudely carved figurines at his side.) When I get stuck, I go outside and make a sandcastle or a snow castle and they act it all out for me.

replies.reply_text: That's a really good idea! So you're writing a novel, eh? That's a big project.
Well, aren't you a clever boots! I won't distract you if you're on a big important scene. Good luck with it!

chatpoints.chat_text: Yeah! This is only the first draft, though, and then I'll need to edit a lot and a lot and a lot more. But I'm going to have it published when I'm thirteen, so that gives me a couple of years to really get it good.

replies.reply_text: You've got ambition! I wish you the best of luck!
It sounds like you've got this all planned out!

chatpoints.chat_text: Thanks! I wish I could get someone else to read it, though. Grandma's sweet, but she's not very good at critique. She always tells me how wonderful it is.

replies.reply_text: I don't understand. Isn't it good to know that your work is good?

chatpoints.chat_text: I need somebody to tell me what's wrong with it, too! I know all about the parts that are good. I wrote it, after all. I made them good on purpose. But I didn't make the bad stuff bad on purpose, so I need to fix that.

replies.reply_text: Oh, so you're looking for more honest feedback. I know some people use writing circles for that. Have you tried looking for something like that?

chatpoints.chat_text: Sorta. I wish I could be somebody's writing apprentice! I could, I don't know, make sure all his pens were around and working, and that he always had enough paper, and do his research for him; and in return he could help me with my writing.

replies.reply_text: Actually, I know a writer on this very isle. His name is Ted, and he lives in Frigid Meadows. What if I go talk to him for you? He might be willing to take you on.
That's an interesting idea. Best of luck finding that kind of situation!
Let's see how it goes!

chatpoints.chat_text: You were going to somebody in Frigid Meadows named Ted to see if he'd take me on as a writing apprentice. Has he given you an answer yet?

replies.reply_text: Er... no, but I'll come back as soon as he has.
Yes, and... I'm afraid he said no.

chatpoints.chat_text: You were going back to see if you could persuade Ted to take me on after all.

replies.reply_text: Oh, right. I'm not afraid of some guy with a stick! Back I go!

chatpoints.chat_text: You were persuading Ted to take me on as his writer's apprentice!

replies.reply_text: Got it!
Best of luck with that novel, buddy!
Aw, heck. You know what, I'm not afraid of him. He was so rude about turning you down that I'm going to go back there and give it another try! You just wait!
That soldier was actually one of Hanska's models. It was very important to her. I don't suppose you know how far it might have gone?

chatpoints.chat_text: Oh... well, the current takes most things southwest here. I can't imagine it would get far in a paper boat. Maybe it washed up somewhere.

replies.reply_text: Yes, if it didn't SINK!

chatpoints.chat_text: Yes, I made it. Why?

replies.reply_text: Did you happen to have a toy soldier you were playing with?

npc_list.short_description: playing with a water-logged bit of paper

chatpoints.chat_text: This? (Looks at the bit of paper in his paws.) Nothin'.

replies.reply_text: It doesn't look like nothing to me. It looks like a bit of paper. Where'd it come from?

chatpoints.chat_text: Why's a bit of somebody's stupid ol' paper boat so important to you, anyhow? That's all it is, a scrap! Ha! (Bats it around.)

replies.reply_text: Paper boat, huh? Did it happen to have a toy soldier in it when it washed up here?

chatpoints.chat_text: So what's it to you if it did?

replies.reply_text: I'm interested, that's all. I don't suppose you know where the toy soldier went?

chatpoints.chat_text: It's possible. Sure, it's possible. (Looks at you coyly.) So what's in it for me? If I know somethin', which I am not sayin' I do.

replies.reply_text: Well, I'm interested, like I said. What would it be worth to you?
How about a trade? This seems to be a pretty deserted little isle. Must be some things that are hard to come by. I bring you something you don't have, you tell me something I don't know.

chatpoints.chat_text: Hmmm. Now, what's it worth to me... that's an awfully good question, you understand. Aw-ful-ly good. You understand it's tough for a rat livin' all on his own out here. I am speakin' of the food. Fish? Sure, I gots plenty of fish. Seaweed? Sure. Scraps from that girl's kitchen? All the time. But there's things a body just can't get hold of.

replies.reply_text: Such as?
I have no idea what you mean.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, I guess you're just gonna have to figure it out! Hah! (Gives the bedraggled remnant of the paper boat a mighty smack with a paw.)

chatpoints.chat_text: A big ol' orange squashy thing.  With the seeds in.  Had one'a them once.

chatpoints.chat_text: Well, that's not my problem. Now buzz off, I have an orange squashy thing to eat.

replies.reply_text: You've been ever so helpful.

chatpoints.chat_text: (Swallows a mouthful of pumpkin.) I know I already told you this, but I'll be nice. You listen this time! "A fish that swims in spirals, as far as it can go."
